title: Small Gestures Of Praise Can Make A Big Impact https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2009/05/25/small-gestures-of-praise-can-make-a-big-impact/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin describes watching a teacher deliver loud, exaggerated praise to a student for a homework assignment, and noticing the student's subtle discomfort despite the teacher's genuine enthusiasm, using the moment to argue that effective praise is not about intensity but about timing and authenticity. He contends that the smallest gestures -- a fist bump, eye contact with a smile, a handshake -- often carry more impact than effusive verbal praise, provided they are genuine and well-timed. He illustrates this with a personal story from his youth hockey career: after making a decisive defensive play in a playoff game, the public celebration went entirely to the team's star scorer, but his coach quietly locked eyes with him from the bench, gave a small fist pump and nod, and that private, understated acknowledgment meant more to him than any public praise could have. He generalizes from both stories that classroom management is shaped by everything a teacher does, including subtle, everyday interactions, not just rules and consequences, and that praise used mindfully and authentically has real power to influence student behavior and academic choices.
points: Effective praise depends less on the intensity or enthusiasm of delivery and more on its timing and authenticity.
Overly effusive, public praise can cause visible discomfort in students, even when the teacher's intentions are genuine.
Small, genuine gestures -- a fist bump, eye contact with a smile, a quiet nod -- are argued to often carry more impact than loud verbal praise.
A personal hockey anecdote illustrates how a private, understated gesture from an admired coach outweighed public team celebration in its lasting impact.
Classroom management is framed as encompassing everything a teacher does, including subtle interactions like praise, not solely rules and consequences.
quotes: Classroom management is more than just rules and consequences. Everything you do as a teacher, from creating your room environment to how you praise your students, affects their behavior.
It was a nice moment, and I admired her enthusiasm—especially so early in the morning. But I’m not sure her praise had the desired effect.

Often, the smallest gestures have the greatest effect—a fist bump, eye contact with a smile, a congratulatory handshake. These brief but genuine moments between a student and his or her teacher can have a powerful impact.
The key to offering praise is not the level of enthusiasm you can muster. Rather, it’s choosing the right time to offer a meaningful commendation.

He locked his intense eyes on mine, pumped his fist ever so slightly, and nodded. His small gesture, unnoticed by my teammates or anyone else in attendance, meant everything to me, and I would have skated through a wall to please him.
Praise can have a strong impact on your students and the behavior and academic choices they make. But it must be used mindfully—at the right time and with a heartfelt touch.
